note: Distilled from this repository's git history and docs/audit/ before the first automated refresh. Each entry's evidence is the commit that made the change.

learned.note: Live progress became its own page behind the menu.
Findings moved out of prose into issues.d/, an append-only ledger that the page folds at build time into Waiting, Tracked and Resolved.
A ledger quote is checked against its cited source, the same way a footnote is.
The page lists every runtime spec and archived change at the pin, as well as the findings.
The spec snapshot was regenerated by hand for v56.10.9.1. Until then, any pin at the new tag made the build refuse.
The spec snapshot regenerates on every release refresh. The residual-obligation history is now drawn from the runtime's git history, back to its first commit, on a logarithmic time axis.
The page was added: the Stockfish analogy, the declared weights and a worked five-obligation example.
Measurement was separated from guarantee. The overclaims were withdrawn with an append-only retraction in issues.d/.
The source links were re-pinned to v56.10.9.1 by hand, and the ratchet link was retargeted to its Lua port.
The source links follow the site pin and are re-anchored by their text. A summary generated from the runtime's history at the pin now closes the page.
The update loop was written down as skills: re-verify every footnote against the stable release, then move the pins.
A footnote may point at a newer daily with @vTAG. That is how a PATH line cites a fix the stable channel does not have yet.

The v56.10.9.1 run corrected 121 footnote targets by hand. Replayed through anchors.py from the v56.9.27.2 tree, 105 of them re-anchor with no person. 101 land on the line the person chose, and 4 differ only in how wide the span is. The other 14 are the ones a person did have to decide: ports from shell to Lua, and quotes the release rewrote.

next_run: Four Level 5 proposals still carry an unchecked operator-review box; see openspec/changes/automated-release-refresh/ for the rule that would retire the mechanical ones.
